hypotheses.statement: Customers wait for answers about refunds because current response times are slow.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, a chatbot that speeds responses directly addresses the root cause.

hypotheses.statement: Waiting is caused by inadequate staffing levels to handle refund inquiry volume.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, adding staff or improving shift coverage would reduce waits more than a chatbot.

hypotheses.statement: Delays stem from customers needing clarification of refund policies that agents cannot quickly convey.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, improving knowledge‑base articles or policy clarity would reduce waits; a chatbot helps only if it can deliver that clarity.

proposal.root_cause: Customers wait for refund answers due to inadequate staffing levels to handle refund inquiry volume.

remedies.description: Increase refund inquiry handling capacity by hiring additional agents or reallocating existing staff to meet inquiry volume.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: Hiring/training exceeds 225 min remaining; reallocation depends on existing spare capacity (see H‑INSUFFICIENT‑STAFFING, U‑STAFFING‑VOLUME‑GAP).
remedies.residual_gap: If hiring, gap persists until new staff are onboarded; if reallocation, gap depends on actual spare capacity.

remedies.description: Reduce refund inquiry volume by publishing clear refund‑policy FAQs and enabling self‑service options.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: FAQ can be published well within 225 min; does not directly fix staffing shortfall (see H‑INSUFFICIENT‑STAFFING, H‑UNCLEAR‑POLICY).
remedies.residual_gap: Volume reduction may not fully eliminate wait if staffing remains insufficient.

proposal.why_agent_needed: An agent is needed to resolve the unknown staffing‑volume gap (U‑STAFFING‑VOLUME‑GAP) and to design/implement the FAQ, requiring judgment and coordination beyond structural changes.
